correctness.rationale: After affine normalization, conditional variance reduces every fixed-profile law to a three-level lower comparison with the same mean. The remaining one-variable ratio is optimized exactly after the odds substitution, and the arithmetic--geometric mean equality condition gives the unique support ratio. The Bhatia--Davis deficit gives the strict upper endpoint, and connectedness yields the full intervals.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources cover broader bounded-variance and finite-universe questions, but none of their stated constraints fixes arbitrary endpoint masses while allowing the mean to vary. Consequently their bounds do not determine the minimum of the Bhatia--Davis efficiency over the present support-shape class.

value.rationale: Bhatia--Davis is a standard bounded-support variance benchmark, and fixed endpoint frequencies are natural extra information in finite categorical and empirical distributions. The theorem gives the exact tightness floor created by that information, a unique three-point worst geometry, and the complete attainable range. The endpoint-only dependence and equal-mass value 2/m make the classification directly interpretable.
